clue.text: Cuts into two parts, taking half a second

indicators.note: the word for parts takes the half-word into its middle, holding it inside

parts.note: bits are small parts or pieces

indicators.note: half of the six-letter word second is its first three letters

explanation.surface: Someone describes splitting something in two, done in a fraction of a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuts into two parts' reads as the definition, but 'parts' belongs to the wordplay as BITS. 'Half a second' is SEC, the first half of SECOND.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect is to divide something into two equal halves, a geometry term.

clue.text: Found unworthy of honour

definitions.meaning: to found something is to establish it on a footing, to set it up

explanation.surface: Someone has been discovered to be undeserving of an award.
explanation.definitionFit: Base as a verb means establish on a foundation; as an adjective it means morally low or contemptible.

clue.text: Outhouse made redundant

definitions.meaning: a small hut or outbuilding in a garden
got rid of, as a firm discards staff or jobs

explanation.surface: A garden outbuilding has been declared surplus to requirements.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden hut is a shed; a company that sheds workers lays them off.

clue.text: Produced original work that's collected

definitions.meaning: wrote music or verse, created it
calm and self-possessed, as in cool, calm and collected

explanation.surface: A writer made new work which has now been gathered into an anthology.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer has composed a piece; a calm person is composed, collected and unflustered.

clue.text: Sign sick note for char

indicators.note: feeling sick or out of sorts, the letters of the word sign are disordered

parts.note: E is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: An instruction to put one's name to a doctor's sick note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sick' looks like illness on a doctor's note, but is the signal to rearrange the first word; the note is musical.
explanation.definitionFit: To char is to scorch or burn the surface slightly, which is what singeing does.

clue.text: Bear right to enter London thoroughfare

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes into the middle of the other word, entering it

parts.note: to bear something is to stand or tolerate it

explanation.surface: Directions telling a driver to keep right to turn into a London street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear right' looks like a driving instruction, but 'Bear' is STAND. The Strand is a famous street in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Strand is a major street in London's West End, running towards the City.

clue.text: How wrestler's brought down may be possibly worth a point

indicators.note: the word worth could possibly be arranged otherwise, so its letters are shuffled

parts.note: a wrestler put on the mat by an opponent has been floored, and in some styles that fall scores
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A wrestling scoring rule about a fighter knocked to the mat earning a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worth a point' reads as scoring, but 'possibly' works on WORTH and the point is a compass point; 'may be' and 'a' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrestler floored by an opponent has been hurled to the mat in a throw.

clue.text: Not against making an enemy

indicators.note: the letters of the first two words are used to make something new

explanation.surface: A paradox: being not against someone still turns them into a foe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' rearranges NOT AGAINST, all ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An antagonist is an opponent or adversary, someone hostile.

clue.text: Notable decrease in volume

parts.note: read as note-able: in music, a gradual lessening of loudness across the notes

explanation.surface: A remarkable drop in sales, or in the size of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notable' seems to mean remarkable, but it hints at musical notes, and volume is loudness.
explanation.definitionFit: A diminuendo is a musical direction for gradually becoming quieter.

clue.text: Very angry with dividing pupils by ability — it's not right

indicators.note: the word for the school practice is said not to contain the abbreviation, so it is dropped

parts.note: streaming is the British school practice of grouping pupils into classes by ability

explanation.surface: Someone furious that schools sort children by ability, calling it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools, streaming is putting pupils into classes by ability. 'it's not right' drops the R from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Steaming is informal for furious, boiling with rage.

clue.text: Not always brief

definitions.meaning: for the time being only, temporarily

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a thing is not invariably short.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro tem is Latin shorthand for pro tempore, meaning temporarily, for now only.

clue.text: Concerning tape being played — it's been on before

parts.note: re means concerning or about

indicators.note: the letters of tape are played with, moved around

explanation.surface: About a recording being played: it has already been aired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being played' suggests the tape running, but signals that its letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeat is a programme broadcast again, something shown previously.

clue.text: Insured vehicle went west

parts.note: covered means insured, as by a policy
a wagon is a horse-drawn or other vehicle

explanation.surface: A vehicle with insurance headed out towards the setting sun.
explanation.walkthrough: Covered wagons carried pioneer settlers westward across America, so the whole clue describes one.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas-topped wagon was the typical transport of American pioneers heading for the frontier.

clue.text: They hope to gain from their betters

definitions.text: They hope to gain from their betters

parts.words: They hope to gain from their betters
parts.note: betters read as people who place bets, from whom the turf accountants profit

explanation.surface: Social climbers hoping to profit from those above them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'betters' looks like superiors, but means people who bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookmakers take wagers and profit when punters lose.

clue.text: Promise loyalty

definitions.meaning: dedication or devotion to a cause

explanation.surface: Two words a politician might ask of supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: A commitment is both an undertaking to do something and dedication to a cause.

clue.text: Nose to nose, perhaps, and alert

indicators.note: the letters might be arranged otherwise, perhaps, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two people face to face, wary and watchful of each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the ten letters of NOSE TO NOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on one's toes is an idiom for being ready and watchful.

clue.text: German number holds out in action

indicators.note: the number word holds the rearranged letters in its middle

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: the letters of out are set in motion, rearranged

explanation.surface: A German player number holds out during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in action' rearranges OUT into UTO, which TEN 'holds'.
explanation.definitionFit: Teuton is an old name for a German, from an ancient Germanic tribe.

clue.text: Born French in the Pyrenees

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the name of the mountain range

explanation.surface: Someone born a Frenchman in the mountains bordering Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pyrenees are the mountains between France and Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Née is the French past participle meaning born, used for a woman's maiden name.

clue.text: The art of the man at the wheel

definitions.text: The art of the man at the wheel

parts.words: The art of the man at the wheel
parts.note: the wheel is a potter's wheel, not a car's steering wheel

explanation.surface: The skill of a driver behind the steering wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wheel' suggests driving, but it is the potter's wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceramics is pottery, the craft of throwing clay on a wheel.

clue.text: I'm after a letter written by Kipling, initially

definitions.text: I'm after a letter written by Kipling, initially

indicators.note: the pronoun phrase comes after the single letter
only the first letter of the author's surname is taken

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a letter in Kipling's handwriting.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines Kim, the 1901 novel by Rudyard Kipling.
explanation.definitionFit: Kim is Rudyard Kipling's novel about an orphan boy in British India.

clue.text: Supported, nevertheless, with locks

parts.note: but means however, nevertheless
tressed means having tresses, locks of hair

explanation.surface: Someone propped up, yet still with a full head of hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' are hair, not door fastenings.
explanation.definitionFit: A buttress is a support built against a wall, so buttressed means propped up.

clue.text: One is often led to use it by mistake

definitions.text: One is often led to use it by mistake

parts.words: One is often led to use it by mistake
parts.note: a pencil's lead makes errors that this rubber then removes

explanation.surface: A tool people are tricked into using by an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'led' hints at pencil lead, and the mistake is what gets rubbed out.
explanation.definitionFit: An eraser is a rubber for removing pencil marks.

clue.text: PM gets down for a siesta, say

parts.note: pm stands for post meridiem, after midday
nap is the soft raised pile on fabric, like down

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister lies down for a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM' suggests the Prime Minister, but is the time of day; 'down' is fluffy pile, not lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is an example of a short sleep after lunch, so 'say' signals an instance.

clue.text: It conveys a sense of courage

definitions.meaning: a fibre carrying sensation impulses to the brain

explanation.surface: Something that communicates a feeling of bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerve carries sensory signals; nerve also means boldness or pluck.

clue.text: They may part with a smile

definitions.text: They may part with a smile

parts.words: They may part with a smile
parts.note: parting here is opening, as the mouth's edges separate when one grins

explanation.surface: Friends who separate on good terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' suggests saying goodbye, but means open slightly.
explanation.definitionFit: When someone smiles, the mouth's fleshy edges often open apart.

clue.text: Hold the fort

definitions.meaning: the central tower or stronghold of a castle

explanation.surface: A command to defend a position, as in hold the fort.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep is to retain; a keep is a castle's strongest tower.

clue.text: Still rings back, nevertheless

parts.note: even means still, as in even more or still more

indicators.note: the letters for rings are read back to front

parts.note: O's, rings being circles shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Bells still ring out again, despite everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns OS (O's, rings) into SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Even so means despite that, all the same, however.

clue.text: Take care — if it changes, it's a trick

indicators.note: the letters of the three words change places, rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning to be careful, because a change would be deceitful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges CARE IF IT; 'Take' and 'it's a' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Artifice is cunning deception, a clever stratagem or ruse.

clue.text: Burlesque star that is ill-disposed

indicators.note: the letters are badly disposed, arranged in a different order

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A burlesque performer who is in a bad mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-disposed' rearranges STAR plus IE.
explanation.definitionFit: Burlesque is a mocking imitation, a form of ridicule like lampoon.

clue.text: Rough sea, upsetting Sue, quietly abates

indicators.note: a rough sea is churned up, so its letters are rearranged
upsetting the name means its letters are disturbed

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction meaning quietly

explanation.surface: A storm at sea frightens Sue, then calms down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough' turns SEA into EAS and 'upsetting' turns SUE into ESU.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease up is to lessen or slacken, as a storm dies down.
